items.text: [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would pull out of Donbas if it joined [[p:NATO]], the first time membership has been tied to territory in the talks. He said Kyiv will not cede land, and would put any deal to a referendum only with security guarantees, a funded army and reconstruction money. He also dismissed [[p:Vladimir Putin]]'s offer of a local truce in Kostiantynivka as a sign Russia cannot take the city.
items.notes: Zelenskyy's account; no US comment in the sources.

items.text: The [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] claims it hit a radar at a US helicopter base in Bahrain early on 15 Nov, state agency IRNA reports. Bahrain says its air defences intercepted several Iranian projectiles and issued its first nationwide alerts since September. On 13 Nov [[p:United States Central Command|CENTCOM]] said it downed two Iranian drones heading for Bahrain and denied an earlier Iranian claim to have hit a US radar.
items.notes: Damage unconfirmed; CENTCOM had not commented on the 15 Nov claim.

items.text: [[p:Donald Trump]] told radio host Hugh Hewitt he would "certainly consider" military force against Cuba and wants to "get Cuba done" before he leaves office, the first time he has put a timeline on it. He said [[p:Marco Rubio]] "would love to do it". Havana has said it is ready for any attack.

Saudi spokesman Turki al-Malki said air defences destroyed two [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh and two drones over the Eastern Region early on 15 Nov. The Houthi-run health ministry says an airstrike on north-eastern Sanaa wounded two women and two children and blames Saudi Arabia.
items.notes: Casualty claim from Houthi ministry, no evidence given.

items.text: Israel says it killed Samir Abu Younis, commander of [[p:Hamas]]'s Rafah Brigade, in an airstrike in southern Gaza; Hamas confirmed his death. His predecessor was killed two months ago.
items.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan

items.text: At the [[e:9th European Political Community Summit]] {{note: The European Political Community is a forum of some 47 European leaders, first convened in Prague in October 2022 on Emmanuel Macron's initiative.}} in Dublin and the informal EU summit that followed, leaders agreed Europe's team for the next round of Ukraine talks will mix EU officials with the E5: France, Germany, the UK, Italy and Poland. They named no single envoy. [[p:Kaja Kallas]] argued she should lead, and the Kremlin said it would weigh European participation only when Europe is "ready to contribute".
items.notes: UK PM Andy Burnham and Canada's Mark Carney attended the EPC on 12 Nov.

items.text: [[p:Ursula von der Leyen]] said a 22nd Russia sanctions package and a plan for Ukraine's 2027 funding will come before the next European Council. The EU has pledged about €45bn of a roughly €70bn gap; Taoiseach [[p:Micheál Martin]] backs a loan.

Slovakia's [[p:Robert Fico]] called [[p:Friedrich Merz]]'s demand that every member state help fund Ukraine "typical blackmail", and [[p:Andrej Babiš]] wrote to [[p:António Costa]] opposing any link between Ukraine money and the 2028–34 budget. Both say they will stay out of any new Ukraine loan. Hungary's [[p:Péter Magyar]] criticised the linkage but, reportedly, not as blackmail. (Fico quote translated from Czech.)

Hungary refused for the third time to approve screening reports for Ukraine's clusters 4 and 5 at the Council's enlargement working party on 10 Nov. Ireland, whose presidency ends on 31 Dec, wants them opened by year-end.

Talks at [[e:2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference|COP31]] in Antalya reached the midpoint with limited progress. Large developing countries resist a cover decision with sectoral targets, African states want adaptation finance tripled to $120bn a year by 2035, and Brazil's [[p:Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva|Lula]] offered to host the third conference on moving away from fossil fuels. Ministers arrive for the second week.

EU gas storage fell to 72.65% on 8 Nov, Gas Infrastructure Europe data show, after peaking below 75% in late October. The [[p:International Energy Agency]] says stocks entered the heating season at their lowest since 2013; Germany was at 61% on 1 Nov. The Commission says emergency measures are not yet needed.
